text.p: CompuServe Corp., the No. 2 online service, Wednesday reported a wider loss for its fiscal fourth quarter, hurt by $9.2 million in one-time special charges and a decline in U.S. subscribers.

Columbus, Ohio-based CompuServe said it lost $18 million, or 19 cents per share, in the quarter ended April 30 vs. a loss of $1.1 million, or 2 cents a share, in the year-ago quarter. Revenues fell to $208 million from $215 million.
Over the last year, the number of U.S. subscribers to its flagship CompuServe Interactive Service has fallen by more than 25 percent to 1.53 million.
The special charges related to a further consolidation of Columbus-area offices and the sale or write-down of some investments in providers of content and technologies.

"Overall, we made progress toward our goal of stabilising earnings and returning CompuServe to profitability," said CompuServe Chairman Frank Salizzoni. He is also chief executive of H&R Block Inc., the tax preparation firm which owns 80.1 percent of CompuServe.
"We expect further improvement in earnings and cash flows, our goal being to reach or exceed the break-even point in earnings sometime in the second half of the current 1998 fiscal year."

For the full fiscal year, CompuServe said it lost $119.8 million, or $1.29 per share, on revenues of $842 million. This compared with a year-ago profit of $49.1 million, or 66 cents per share, on revenues of $793 million.
Founded in 1969, CompuServe is the second-largest online service after America Online and provides online and Internet access through its CompuServe Interactive and Sprynet businesses.
Salizzoni said a continued decline in U.S. subscribers to the CompuServe Interactive online and Internet service, and its impact on fourth-quarter revenues, were disappointing.
"The decline in our CompuServe Interactive subscriber base was due in part to the reduction of U.S. direct marketing during the quarter," he said.

CompuServe Interactive subscribers in the United States fell 127,000 to 1.53 million at the end of the quarter from 1.65 million three months earlier. That compared with a peak of 2.1 million subscribers at the end of the fiscal fourth quarter last year, a spokesman said.

Global CompuServe Interactive subscribers fell to 2.77 million from 2.89 million during the fourth quarter and compared with 3.2 million a year earlier. European subscribers rose 19,000 to 892,000 in the fourth quarter and compared with 694,000 a year earlier.
As of April 30, CompuServe said it had a total of 5.37 million direct and licensed subscribers, up from 5.34 million as of Jan. 31. CompuServe stock ended unchanged at $10.125 on Nasdaq.
